Sunday XC Course-

What hill are we climbing?

 

The Carson City Everest Challenge will climb up Kings Canyon via King St from the intersection with Longview to the trailhead parking lot at the end of the paved road. The segment is 1.45 miles long and gains 552 ft of elevation. The average gradient is 7.2% but there are section of 12% grades.

 

How long will it take?

 

Very fit riders will take on the order of 10 to 12 hours. For recreational riders the event could take quite a bit longer. We will have the course open from 3:00AM to 9:00 PM for a total of 18 hours.

 

How hard is this challenge?

 

A full Everest Challenge is a serious endurance event that requires a lot of training ahead of time. You should be able to handle being on the bike for a full day and have a good set of climbing legs. The Tour of the California Alps (The Death Ride) is another local event that would provide excellent training for the Everest Challenge.

Is the road closed to traffic during the event?

 

The road will be closed to the general public from 6AM to 6PM. During this time the only vehicles allowed on the road are King St residents, event staff vehicles, and emergency services vehicles. If family members or friends want to spectate, they are more than welcome to ride bikes up to the upperaid station, or arrange for a ride with event staff.

 

Are there aid stations?

 

Yes! There will be a full-service aid station in the trailhead parking lot at the top of King St. There will also be a water only aid station at the bottom of King St. Both aid stations will be staffed from 3AM to 11PM and have basic bicycle repair equipment.

 

What food will the aid station have?

 

The full-service aid station will be stocked all day long with water, carb drinks, energy gels, potato chips, cookies, fruit, PBJ sandwiches, various candies and sodas. We will also have catered sandwiches available for lunch from 12:00 – 2:00, as well as popsicles throughout the afternoon, and ramen noodles

and hot drinks in the evening.

 

Are there bathrooms on the course?

 

Yes, there is a set of bathrooms in the trailhead parking lot. We will also have a port-a-potty at the lower aid station.

Join us for the VeloPigs Beer and Bicycle Social Club’s 6th annual Oink At The Moon! This event is a non-competitive NIGHT GRAVEL ride taking place on the rural farm roads of western Loudoun County. 

 

Oink at the Moon Roots! 

Oink At The Moon originally began as a single, standalone charity ride in October 2020. VeloPigs’ founder, Kasey Clark, attempted to ride every gravel road in Loudoun County (over 285 miles!) in a single day. The ride was a success and raised significant funds for America’s Routes, a Loudoun-based non-profit whose mission is to protect and preserve these historic roads.

 

In 2021, to pay homage to Kasey’s big ride, the VeloPigs organized a night gravel century and opened it to club members. Each year since, Oink At The Moon has continued to grow into one of the highlights of the Loudoun County cycling calendar. It is a true grassroots gravel event, and we would love for you to come share this experience with us!

 

This year we are again being hosted by longtime VeloPig and ride leader, Brian Holesapple. He is graciously allowing us to start and end our ride at his property near Philomont.

 

Even if you’ve ridden Loudoun’s gravel before (perhaps every Saturday morning with the VeloPigs), riding at night completely changes the experience. Prepare for an exhilarating new adventure, traversing some of the lost corners of the county and camaraderie you can only find on a ride like this!

 

Ride Details

  • Routes and parking information will be emailed to you when you register.

  • The ride will take place on open roads, both gravel and paved. 

  • The ride starts at 6:30 pm, approximately half an hour before sunset, and will finish well after dark.

  • Participants are expected to follow all rules of the road and act as responsible stewards for the sport of cycling. 

  • The route will be unmarked, though GPS routes will be emailed upon registration. 

  • Road conditions will range from hardpack (almost as smooth as pavement) to sometimes deep, loose gravel with potholes and washboard. 

  • We recommend at least a 32mm tire width, though 38+ mm is ideal. We also recommend tubeless tires - changing a flat in the dark is not easy!

 

Route Options

This year, we have three route options (63 miles, 46 miles, and 30 miles – routes will be sent when you register). Unlike our Saturday club rides, these groups will not have ride leaders and are NOT no-drop. Meaning, these are drop rides. Riders are encouraged, but not required, to stick with their ride group.

The VeloPigs follow the “Mullet Protocol” for all our rides: 

  • Business at the front, party at the back. 

    • The Business is 63 miles, and the group will ride at an average speed of 16+ mph. 

    • Business Casual is 46 miles and will average 14.5-16 mph. 

    • Party Pace is 30 miles and will average 12-14.5 mph. 

  • Please register for the route and pace that will best suit your riding abilities.

  • Riders are asked to stage 5-10 minutes before the ride begins. 

  • Groups will roll out at 5-minute intervals to avoid congesting the small roads with too many riders.

 

Rest Stops

  • There are no designated rest stops, though each route passes by at least one convenience store:

    • The Business: Middleburg Safeway at mile 11, The Plains Sunoco at mile 29, and Middleburg Safeway again at mile 45.

    • Business Casual: Middleburg Safeway at mile 11, and Middleburg Safeway again at mile 29.

    • Party Pace: Purcellville 7-Eleven at mile 21.

  • Riders are expected to bring their own hydration and nutrition, and/or money to purchase more along the way.

     

Most Importantly - Food & Drink!

  • Pizza, beer (21+), and VeloPigs swag are included with entry will be provided after the ride. 

 

The Fine Print

  • Riders are expected to have appropriate fitness, equipment, and bike handling skills to complete their selected route.
  • Helmets, headlights, and taillights are REQUIRED!
    • We recommend staying with a riding buddy in case of mechanical or light issues.
  • Mechanical support will be provided before the ride by VeloPigs’ bike shop sponsor, Plum Grove Cyclery.
  • SAG support will be available for riders who experience mechanical difficulties and are unable to complete the ride.
  • Registration may be edited or transferred at no charge up until the day before the event, however refunds will not be granted.
  • If you would like to participate in this ride but are unable to cover the registration cost, please contact the Event Director.

 

Lastly, some friendly advice (because this has been an issue every year): It may be warm at the beginning of the ride, but it will get cold quickly when the sun sets! 

DRESS FOR THE COLD TEMPS AT THE END OF THE RIDE, NOT THE WARM TEMPS AT THE BEGINNING. Trust us on this….

Bring a big ol’ trash bag, put your garbage in your big ol’ trash bag, put your big ol’ trash bag in your car, put your car in your driveway, and put your trash in your trashcan at home. Join Us for an Epic Day on the Gravel!

The Jersey Gravel Grinder returns in 2026 for another unforgettable ride through the backroads, dirt lanes, and hidden gems of the Garden State. Whether you’re chasing the sunrise or chasing a new PR, this is Jersey’s own gravel adventure — and it’s calling your name.

Early Bird Bonus – Free Custom Jersey!

To thank our amazing community of Adventurers, the next 50 riders to sign up for May 3 event by December 8, 2025 will receive a limited-edition 2026 Jersey Gravel Grinder Bike Jersey — a $75 value, free!
Don’t wait — these will go fast, and you’ll want to be rocking the official look on ride day.

The Ride: Gravel, Grit & Glory

Our signature JGG routes deliver a perfectly mixed all-surface adventure — from smooth tarmac to gritty gravel, rugged dirt, and maybe even a bit of singletrack on the Mega & Mega XL courses. Expect 45%–75% unpaved terrain, all clearly marked with arrow signs at every turn.

Prefer tech over trail signs? You’ll also get free access to our RideWithGPS event account, with downloadable FIT and GPX files, plus visual and audio cues to guide you every pedal stroke.

Ride Your Way – Enduro Style

This isn’t just a race — it’s an experience. Compete for the fastest combined time on timed segments rather than your total ride time. You’ll see clear signage marking the Approach, Start, and End of each Strava segment, so you know exactly when to hammer and when to chill.
Go full gas or soak in the scenery — it’s your adventure, your pace.

Each edition of JGG brings something new — from pint glasses and mugs to water bottles, socks, neck gaiters, and arm warmers. For 2026, we’re crafting something extra special. Stay tuned for the reveal!

!!!!!!!Start time notes!!!!!

In an effort to offer a safer and more fun race environment for all participants we are now starting Cat 2 and Cat 3 racers after Cat 1 and E Bikes have completed one lap. This greatly reduces conflict between very fast cat 1 and E Bike racers passing novice racers by nearly eliminating lap traffic. The posted start time of 12:40m for cat 2 & 3 is approximate. We will begin releasing the remaining cat 2 & 3 waves after Cat 1 racers go through scoring. Know your wave number!

10am Cat3 Jr. Novice Races

You may have noticed that we are doing Cat3 Jr novice races early in the day and be asking "hey, what's up with that?" We want to give Jr's, and particularly novice Jr's the best race day experience we can. Separating the Jr. novice races to an earlier start allows us to do 3 things:

  • Fewer racers on course for the race.
  • For families where the one or both parents also race it gives the parents a chance to spectate and cheer their kids.
  • Novice Jr's get their own start, with more people cheering and spectating. Bring the cowbells!

USA Cycling Licenses, and NOMBS Series Championship rules & eligibility:

NOMBS is proud to be bringing a USAC sanctioned series to Ohio and be hosting the official USA Cycling Ohio MTB Championship. Partnering with USA Cycling helps us offer you a great series with structure, consistent categories & scoring, good insurance for landowners, and allows an opportunity for riders with goals outside Ohio to earn USAC points. 

USA Cycling Race Age:

 Your “race age” is the age you will be on December 31st. This rule exists so that a person does not have to change the age group they are entering partway through a race season. 

NOMBS Series Championship Eligibility rules:

  1. A rider must have a current USA Cycling License (need not reside in Ohio).
  2. Must race in the season finale race.
  3. Scored on best 5 races.
  4. In the event of a points tie the season final race is the tie breaker.

Complete series rules can be found here.

THE BATTLES TO BIKES STORY:

 

For over 20 years, Jim Yurek (The Bike Lab owner) served his local western Pennsylvania communities as a police officer and in those decades, time and again he interacted with United States veterans in need. At the point he intercepted these American heroes, they were often deep in the throes of trauma, anguish and the feeling that America had forgotten about them. Many of these veterans struggled with mental illness, substance abuse, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder and physical injuries related to military combat. Following his retirement from law enforcement, Jim made a significant career change in 2021 and opened The Bike Lab.

 
Jim soon made friends with Drew, an Army veteran and bike enthusiast, and through the sharing of his harrowing military stories, spurred Jim’s quest to find a way to serve local veterans through The Bike Lab. The idea of Battles to Bikes was born. 


In the fall of 2021, a small but passionate group joined forces as the Board of Directors for Battles to Bikes. The five-member Board is composed of business leaders, bike enthusiasts and local community members with a shared vision to serve the veterans of western Pennsylvania. One of the Board members is also an Army veteran. Drew serves as a Board Advisor.

 
In October 2022, Battles to Bikes was designated a 501c3 non-profit organization by the Internal Revenue Service. Starting out slow as many non-profits do, the initial funds of Battles to Bikes were raised through small raffles and a 62-mile paid-registration group bike ride event on the Great Allegheny Passage (GAP) in July 2022. Using an anonymous application process, Battles to Bikes – supported by The Bike Lab – was able to gift its first mountain bike, a Giant, to a local veteran on Saturday, November 12, 2022 in honor of Veterans Day.

 
In May 2023, Battles to Bikes presented a new Giant Cypress to our friends at Pittsburgh Warriors, a military service-connected hockey team for disabled veterans. Pittsburgh Warriors gifted the bicycle to veteran / Pittsburgh Warriors participant, Josh, who used his new rig to train for and participant in the July 2023 Healing Ride, a GAP trail ride from Pittsburgh to Washington, D.C. Since the inception of Battles to Bikes, we have gifted over 12 bicycles to local veterans.

 
Be sure to watch the Battles to Bikes’ Facebook page for fundraising events and group rides!

EventName: Randy Nixon's CrosstoberFest at Frey's Farm
EventNotes:
Randy Nixon's CrosstoberFest at Frey's Technical Guide 2026

In Memory of Randy Nixon: 

  

 

All USA Cycling Cyclocross rules apply.

  • Held under USA Cycling permit.
  • For age-graded races, Racing Age is defined as your age on December 31, 2027.
  • Mountain bikes are allowed, but bar ends are NOT permitted and must be removed.
  • There will be 1 double pit on the course.
  • Event will be held rain or shine.

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  

All registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Addtional entries are offered at $20 when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $25 for Juniors for race day registration, to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table.

This page will re-open for day-of registration by 8:30pm on Friday;  check-in will open by 8:30 AM on the day of the event.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race.  There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

U19 Men & Women may race in any class they qualify for by Cyclocross category, but remain eligible for the Junior entry fee.  U19 Men and Women ONLY may use coupon code CFX2026_JRS at checkout to receive the Junior pricing; for race day entry, the day-of surcharge will be applied as appropriate.  Any current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted free entry, but must wear their national jersey in the class in which it was won.

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry in all races other than Li'l Belgians.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license (or a printed Authorization to Ride) showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

The Venue: 

Crosstoberfest is located at Frey's Farm which is Frederick County's first operational farm brewery, located in Mount Airy, Maryland. Frey's was established in 2012 by Air Force vet, Adam Frey, and their beautiful tasting room opened in early 2019 inside a fully-renovated, 200-year-old bank barn. NO outside alcohol permitted at the event venue.  

The Hosts:

Bluemont Connection was founded in 2016 by a group of four friends who wanted to race cyclocross together. Since then, the team has grown to more than 20 members who love gravel adventure, as well as CX. Bluemont hosts the popular Tuesday Towpath ride from Georgetown each week and also puts on B3 in Lost River, WV each spring.

Sportif Coaching Group/AVC is a Mid-Atlantic based cycling club with teams based in Maryland and Virginia.  Members of the team participate in nearly all disciplines of cycling but the majority are focused on Cyclocross. The club is sponsored by Sportif Coaching Group, Hunts End Remodeling, Patapsco Bicycles, Shulman/Rogers, and Element Sports.

Neutral Support by Patapsco Bicycles

 

Electronic Chip Timing by Insight Timing Services

 

Warmups:  The course will be open for inspection and warm-up approximately 15 minutes prior to each event. Warming up on the course during an event is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated. DQ & forfeiture of entry fee will result.

Novice Racer Guided Course Preview:  This on-bike preview is for Novice racers who will be competing in the 12:00pm Novice race block. You will be guided through the race course by experienced local racers and coaches. This begins promptly at 10:30am at the Staging Grid. 

Course Description:  Located at Frey's Farm in Mount Airy, Maryland, our course includes grass, gravel, hard-pack dirt, soft soil, and various barriers. The Brewery is a scenic venue for a race and offers wonderful spectating opportunities, with nearly the entire course visible from the Brewery's spacious deck.

Course Preview:  The course will be open for preview starting at 8:00am until just before the first race and then briefly between races. 

Start Line Protocol:  Racers must report to the holding pen adjacent to the starting grid for staging 15 minutes before the start of their race. 

Categories listed with the same start time may start up to 30 second apart at the discretion of the Race Director and Chief Official. 

Staging:  All races will reserve up to 1 spot in the first row and up to 1 spot in the second row, which are to be used for promoters' discretion call-ups. Otherwise staging for riders registered prior to the close of early registration is based on a rider's Crossresults Rankings as of 9:30am on Friday, September 25 2026. If multiple pre-registered riders in the same race have the same Crossresults Ranking those riders will additionally be staged based on their registration date & time. Riders who register after the close of early registration at 8:30am on Friday, September 25 2026 will be staged after the riders who registered early based on the their order of check-in on race day. 

Lapped Riders: Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leaders. Per USA Cycling Rule 4G.: Lapped riders must yield the course to overtaking riders as quickly, efficiently and as safely as possible. Overtaking riders shall announce themselves sufficiently in advance of attempting to pass. Both overtaking and lapped riders shall be jointly responsible for a safe pass.

Pit:  There will be one double-sided pit on the course. Please remove your equipment immediately following your race to make room for others. 

Field Limits:  For the races with combined fields the 150 field limit is for the COMBINED field, not for each individual field. BikeReg has been set up so that once the limit has been reached for the combined field registration will close for each of the individual fields within the combined field.

Podiums and results reporting: 

All podiums will feature the top 5 finishers eligible for that specific podium. Podiums will be held as soon as possible following the end of the 15-minute protest period for results. 

The following races will have multiple podiums:

Masters 50+/60+/70+ Open. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 50+, 60+, and 70+ finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Masters 40+/50+ Cat. 4/Novice. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 40+ and 50+ finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Junior 11/12 & 13/14 Men. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 11/12 and 13/14 finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Junior 11/12 & 13/14 Women. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 11/12 and 13/14 finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Junior 9-10 Men & Women. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 9-10 men and 9-10 women finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Master Women 40+/50+/60+/70+ Open. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 40+, 50+, 60+, and 70+ finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Prizes:

All cash and prizes will be awarded based on the information listed above.

Races listed as Prizes/3 will pay merchandise prizes to the top 3 finishers.

Races listed as Prizes/5 will award merchandise prizes to the top 5 finishers for each of that race's podiums.

Races listed as Medals/3 will award medals to the top 3 finishers.

Races listed as Medals/3 + Prizes/3 will award medals and merchandise prizes to the top 3 finishers.

Races listed as Medals/3 + Prizes/5 will award medals to the top 3 finishers and merchandise prizes to the top 5 finishers for each of that race's podiums

Common Courtesy: Please be respectful of the environment and its inhabitants. We are guests of the brewery and there will be other customers present on race day. We would like to remind everyone that we all have a responsibility to leave the race course cleaner than we found it. All refuse should be discarded into appropriate containers. Any rider found illegally discarding objects on the brewery grounds, the roads leading to and from the race course, and/or the race course itself will be dealt with accordingly (see USA Cycling Rule 3B10, which states in part – ‘All riders must respect nature and the environment throughout the course and not to pollute the site. Riders may not discard materials that are not biodegradable; they may pass or throw such material in designated green zones or to support personnel in places far from any bystanders. It is strictly forbidden to throw waste directly onto the course or outside the areas as noted above [fine and/or disqualification for littering].'. Trash containers will be available for rider’s to use at registration.

Sportsmanlike Conduct:  The Chief Referee and Race Director expect ALL spectators and riders to act like responsible adults. Use of profanity and blatant unsportsmanlike conduct will not be tolerated. This is a family-friendly event and we are not the only people at the venue so please be courteous to venue patrons and staff.

Other Rules:  No outside alcohol permitted at the venue. Dogs must be kept on leash at all times. 

For more information and questions, please email:  glennpstevens@gmail.com

Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! Ride start times vary by season to give us the best trail conditions and safest experience—May through September we roll out at 9:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT. We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available.

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 7:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

EventNotes:
Martha's Ride 2026 Benefiting The Martha Fund — Building Playgrounds Across Pittsburgh, Honoring Those Who Serve

Martha's Ride honors FBI Special Agent Martha Dixon, killed in the line of duty on November 22, 1994, and stands in support of the law enforcement community that shares her legacy. Inspired by the Police Unity Tour, this annual ride travels from her name on the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Wall in Washington, D.C. to the Martha Dixon FBI Field Office in Pittsburgh — 329 miles along the C&O Canal Towpath and Great Allegheny Passage. Every dollar raised builds playgrounds for Pittsburgh's kids in the communities our officers protect every day.

THREE WAYS TO RIDE

Endurance Ride — Sept 28–Oct 2 329 miles over five days. Depart the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Wall in Washington, D.C. on Monday, September 28 and finish at the Martha Dixon FBI Field Office in Pittsburgh on Friday, October 2. Overnight stops in Harper's Ferry, WV (Clarion Inn); Hancock, MD; Cumberland, MD (Fairfield Inn); and Ohiopyle, PA. A SAG vehicle and trailer accompany the full route with limited mechanical support, nutrition, and gear transport. Full-service bike shops are available along the route for serious mechanical issues. Riders arrange their own lodging — recommended accommodations provided at confirmation.

Pittsburgh Day Ride — Oct 3 (10-Mile) Start at Southside Riverfront Park under the Birmingham Bridge and roll out along the South Side trail. Sweeping views of the Pittsburgh skyline across the Monongahela make this one of the most scenic rides in the city — flat, welcoming, and perfect for families and first-timers. Finish at the Martha Dixon bench near Hot Metal Bridge where a Pittsburgh Police escort leads the group back down Carson Street to the park for the official finish. Open to all fitness levels. Bring the family.

EventName: CX School - Free Beginner CX Clinics
EventNotes:
Bike racing can be a bit scary and very little of that fear can be from the actual racing

Knowing how call-ups work, how to handle your bike, pre-race prep, and maintenance are all things that can be intimidating for someone just getting into the sport. We're hosting free weekly cyclocross clinics (what we call CX School) for beginners to cover all that stuff, and more. This weekly series will focus on different topics each week - but we will revisit things to bring everything together and get new people up to speed. We hope you leave our clinics not just feeling like you learned a bit about bike racing, but have also made new friends that will help you on your new adventure!

This is beginner's clinic for people who have either never raced at all, haven't raced cross before, or are just wanting to refine their skills for this coming season. Bring whatever bike+helmet you have, and something to drink. Plan for about an hour of instruction+ride time at the park. 

We'll be meeting at 6pm on the following dates, rain or shine (unless the rain is a bad storm)

  • August 4th, 2026
  • August 11th, 2026
  • August 18th, 2026
  • August 25th, 2026
  • September 1st, 2026
  • September 8th, 2026
  • September 15th, 2026
  • September 22nd, 2026
  • September 29th, 2026


If you see one of the CX School leaders at a race, don't hesitate to say "hi" or ask any questions. We're here/there to help you out!
 

Why is this free?

It's expensive enough to get into racing as it is, and learning more about it shouldn't add to that burden. If you're worried about the quality of instruction I've been helping people ride and race better since 2013. I've led dozens of free clinics for cyclocross and mountain biking, started the Lincoln, NE chapter of Nebraska DEVO (kids mountain biking program) and led instruction there as well. I'm just getting back into racing after some health issues and love to share what I know about bikes and welcome others into the sport.

Cyclocross Race Training at Hale Education. 

Driving Directions: Hale’s South Entrance – next to 573 Dover Road, Westwood, MA, 02090 

We have fields, stairs, gravel, a sandpit, and a beach to ride, with fewerot rocks and roots than many of Hale's other trails.  

You can expect two twenty-minute heats and a multiple-lap course. 

Support MTB at Hale 

Mountain bikers of all ages are drawn to Hale’s rugged, varied terrain just miles from Boston’s city line, and we’ve been eagerly expanding youth mountain biking program over the past five years. 

Hale MTB Camp focuses on skill-building and ride time for an existing community of young mountain bikers. Youth MTB Club is growing that community through a fantastic team of volunteer coaches who coordinate recreational rides and opportunities to participate in races and events throughout New England. Intrepid Academy at Hale students also enjoy time on the trails as part of their semester at Hale. 

We’re thrilled with our progress and are helping hundreds of riders advance, but with your help, we can do more. 

Thank you for supporting MTB opportunities for youth by making your donation today. 

About Hale 

Hale is a nonprofit organization that serves nearly 16,000 people annually. We count on donations from people like you to help us provide an outdoor experience to the children in Greater Boston. Your gift today will help us continue to run great programs like this one, steward the land for our community, and ensure Greater Boston’s kids have transformational camp experiences. 

By registering for Hale’s events and programs, you consent to its privacy policy, media policy, and refund policies.

The 2026 Mid Atlantic Super Series consists of 3 separate individual and team competitions in 3 separate forms of mountain bike racing - Cross Country, Endurance and Enduro series.  This is for Series Registration only and does not include any race registrations. Registering for the series is for series points, team points and end-of-season awards and winners jerseys. 

E-Bikes - Some races do have an e-bike non-MASS class. For these races an e-bike is only permitted in the e-bike class. For races without an e-bike class e-bikes are not permitted.

2026 MASS race schedule can be found by clicking HERE to go to the MASS website

Important note - Your Racing Age is determined by your age on December 31st of the current year.  To explain –  for classes like U19 (Under 19) the racer CANNOT turn 19 in the current race year.  Same for U15 (Under 15), the racer CANNOT turn 15 in the current year. Parents - please take note of this when registering your juniors for the races.

Please take a minute to read the Series Race Rules

The MASS website contains the important details about how we run the series. Topics such as the Series Guidelines, General Rules, Upgrade Rules and XC Payouts can be found at

masuperseries.com

MASS registered racers are competing for end-of-season champions jerseys and individual and team awards in the XC and Endurance races. In order to be entered into the MASS series competitions participants must register for the series here and be assigned a series plate number.  Series Registration is a requirement for the series and we will continue to use permanent series number plates with timing chips in them for XC and multi-lap Endurance races.

IMPORTANT - You must register yourself for the series and each race using YOUR BikeReg profile. We cannot have team directors register their team riders all at once because that will cause a major scoring problem. This is because when you create your BikeReg profile there is a unique Racer ID number associated with you and your profile. You do not see this number but it is downloaded for series registration and for each race registration and it is what allows the scoring system to recognize you and assign you your series plate for each race as well as score you properly when race results are imported into our scoring system. One comment for parents that register themselves as well as their children. This can be done, there is a way to have multiple racers in your BikeReg profile. Contact tech support at BikeReg for details. When you register for each race on BikeReg make sure you use your BikeReg profile and do not register as a “guest” or you will not be assigned your series plate and that will cause all kinds of problems.

Series Registration is not required to participate in any MASS races. This registration DOES NOT register you for any of the races. This registration DOES register you for the MASS series of competions - XC, Endurance & Enduro

Series plate. As is the past this is the basis for all scoring for most races (all XC races). If you do not race with your series plate you will not be scored properly at the race and you will not be scored properly for the series. Do not forget your series plate. If you do forget it or lose it you must let us know BEFORE you race with a non-series plate or you will not be scored for the series. Some Endurance and Enduro races will not use series plates.

Team Topics. The only way to earn series points for your team is to be registered for the series and have your team director add you to your team when they do their team registration. Team registration will be done by team directors requesting an access code to be able to login to the MASS Team Registration site and assign team members. It is that registration process that ties you to the team scoring. We do recommend you include your team name in your BikeReg profile so that team name shows up in your results on-line but that team name has nothing to do with getting the points for your team. If you register for a race at the race your team name will not be entered into the timing system because there is not enough time to do that. That means your team name will not show in the on-line results. You will however still earn your team points as long as you raced with your series plate. Check the MASS website for the latest information. 

Most MASS races do not require a USAC license for any classes. Check the race-specific BikeReg page.

   
This MASS series registration is separate from individual race registration.  Any questions please contact support@masuperseries.com.  Visit www.masuperseries.com for more information.  There are no refunds for any reason.

EventNotes:
The Tour de Pines, sponsored by the Pinelands Alliance celebrates Pinelands Month in October.  The ride is co-sponsored by the Outdoor Club of South Jersey

This year we offer four single-day self-guided bicycle tours on the paved roads of the New Jersey Pinelands.  There is no other bike ride like this in New Jersey!

Participants register for each day & route they want to participate in; if you register for multiple days, you will automatically receive an entry fee discount on your additional days, if you register for them at the same time.  For example, your initial ride will cost $60, and your additional rides will cost $20 each.  Each of the first 200 participants will receive a complimentary Tour de Pines Ball Cap prior to your first ride (one per person, regardless of the numbers of days you register for). 

Proceeds benefit the Pineland Alliance (PPA).  Founded in 1989, the PPA is a private, nonprofit organization dedicated to saving the Pinelands of New Jersey.  PPA protects the land, water, plants, wildlife, and historic resources of New Jersey’s Pinelands National Reserve.  The PPA engages thousands of people each year in actions to protect the wildest place in New Jersey.

All routes start & finish in the same location; participants provide their own transportation, food, and lodging as these are unsupported rides.  Although the rides are self-supported & self-guided, we will provide each participant with:

  • Cue Sheets
  • GPS Files
  • Free Access to the Ride with GPS App
  • Instructions that contain details about the rides


Day 1: Thursday, October 1, 2026
RIDE LIKE THE DEVIL
Start/Finish location: Renault Winery, 72 North Bremen Avenue, Egg Harbor City, NJ 08215 

29 and 55-mile routes are available

This ride will take you to several historic and legendary sites in the Pine Barrens. The Long Route will visit Leeds Point – the birthplace of the Jersey Devil; other highlights include Port Republic and Oyster Creek, and side trips may be made to the Edwin B. Forsythe National Wildlife Refuge, Chestnut Neck (site of a battle fought in the Revolutionary War), places that are not too far off of the route. The short route follows the long route through some very dense and iconic areas within the pines. Pre-Ride Technical Support by Bikes by the Beach of Brigantine, NJ.
 

Day 2: Friday, October 2, 2026
WHITESBOG DISCOVERY
Start/Finish location: Whitesbog Village 120 W Whites Bogs Rd, Browns Mills, NJ 08015

26 and 52-mile routes are available

This ride departs from Historic Whitesbog Village, and travels through Greenwood Forest WMA,Chatsworth, Brendan Byrne State Forest, New Lisbon, Hanover Furnace, and Joint Base Fort Dix – McGuire.  It also passes Deborah Hospital and Mirror Lake in Browns Mills.  The long route gives riders an opportunity to stop at Pine Barrens landmark Hot Diggidy Dog in Chatsworth.  Pre-Ride Technical Support by Aistriu of Marlton, NJ. 


Day 3: Saturday, October 3, 2026
EDGE OF THE PINES
Start/Finish location: Parvin State Park 701 Almond Rd, Pittsgrove, NJ 08318

24, 34, and 51-mile routes are available

New for 2026, we take you to the Edge of the Pines, starting and finishing at Parvin State Park.  A hidden gem of the region the park combines rich history with abundant natural beauty.  This ride takes us further west than we’ve ventured before, past extensive stretches of farmland, and into small towns like Alloway and Elmer as we circle around Pittsgrove.

 

Day 4 – Sunday, October 4, 2026
BARREN BACKROADS
Start/Finish location: Pinelands Alliance 17 Pemberton Rd, Southampton NJ 08088

29 and 53-mile routes are available

Sunday’s ride departs from the Pinelands Alliance offices in Southampton, NJ, and winds through the scenic farm fields of Southampton before heading into Tabernacle and Chatsworth. Along the way, you’ll experience quiet back roads and long, straight stretches lined with towering pines.

The long route ventures into Chatsworth, the “Capital of the Pine Barrens” and the Cranberry Capital of New Jersey, where you’ll have a second opportunity to stop at the legendary Hot Diggidy Dog for a bite to eat. From there, you’ll continue to Tabernacle, where you’ll meet up with the short course, and you can choose to stop at either Nixon’s General Store or Russo’s Market—two well-known Pinelands establishments—for refreshments.

After taking in the area’s scenic farmland, the route heads back toward Southampton with a final stretch through the historic village of Vincentown before returning to the Pinelands Alliance.

As this ride serves as the Grand Finale of the 2026 Tour de Pines, we’re offering post-ride food & drinks within the Alliance’s renovated barn. Spellbound Brewing of Mount Holly, NJ provides beer for the post-ride festivities.  

Pre-Ride Technical Support by Erlton Bike Shop of Cherry Hill, NJ

 

Conditions of Entry:

  • All entries are final; no refunds. Entries are not transferable.  Please don't ask.
  • The first 200 individual registrants will receive a complimentary Tour de Pines Ball Cap
  • All merchandise orders and event premiums  (except special order jerseys) must be picked up at the event, including the Ball cap.
  • All participants are required to check in prior to each day’s ride. All participants must sign the event waiver and release during the registration process.  Parents/legal guardians must complete the waiver for minors.  All minors must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian at all times. 
     
  • The rides will be held rain or shine.  Normal amounts of rain will not cancel the rides.  However, in the event of Extreme Weather (such as named storms, or Official Weather Warning), other emergency, impassable roads, or other situations beyond the organizers’ control, the organizers reserve the right to cancel the event or reschedule it to a date of their convenience.  If you cannot attend the rescheduled date, entry fee refunds will not be issued.
  • Should the event be cancelled for reasons of force majeure, entry fees will not be refunded.
     
  • The roads are open to vehicular traffic; all rules of the road must be obeyed.  Participants are responsible for their own safety and for knowing and complying with New Jersey’s applicable laws and vehicle codes
  • Participants should ride in a safe and courteous manner; please stay to the right, except when passing.  NJ Traffic Guidelines suggest cyclists ride Single File.
  • All bicycles must have at least 1 working brake
  • All riders must wear a helmet that meets CPSC, ANSI and/or Snell (or similar standards).
  • Wearing headsets or earbuds are prohibited.

E-Bike Users are required to be familiar with NJ E-Bike laws, and are solely responsible for their own compliance.  Please note that we may not be able to support or SAG large or heavy E-Bikes.

EventName: Sorry Honey, I've Gotta Work Late
EventNotes:
Sorry Honey, I've gotta work late! 

REGISTRATION:
We encourage racers to register early.  We are offering series entry, at a discount, or you can sign up for individual event dates.

COURSE INFO:
All races will be located in Forest Hill Park, Richmond, VA. 

Cross course: the lap will be approximately one mile in length using a combination of surfaces that may include grass, blacktop and dirt.   What type of bike?  We don't care...race your cross, mountain or gravel bike. 

Lapped Rider:  If you are lapped you can continue to race, unlike some cyclo cross races. Once the race leader finishes the required number of laps, remaining riders will will be done once they complete their current lap.  The event will be scored by number of laps completed, then by time.

AWARDS: 
There will be series awards after 3rd race.  To be eligible for prizes, you must enter and race all three events.  

DISTANCE/TIME:
All races will be about 45 minutes.  Our goal is for the 1st pace overall to race close to 45 minutes.  All racers then will finish their current lap once the leader finishes. There will be a countdown lap count at the start/finish.  Lapped racers will not be removed from the course!  All racers will be able to continue to the finish of the event!

NUMBER OF LAPS:
Race organizers will determine numbers of laps based on average time per lap of leaders.  Once laps times are established there will be l lap counter counting down the laps.  This number will be reduced by 1 each time the leader crosses the line.  Note that the number can change by 2 if the leader passes you during any given lap. We will ring a bell for riders to signal "one to go". Historically, the winner completes 11 to 12 laps in the 45 minute window.

 

DONATION:
Donations will go to the local trail working groups (RVA MORE) earmarked to maintain the trails at Forest Hill Park.  Please donate a few bucks during registration.

RAIN OR WET CONDITIONS
To protect/secure our use of the park, we will postpone or cancel a race in the event of rain or wet conditions.  Don't let this prevent you from registering early.  We are happy to transfer fees to another runriderace event.

Course set up
I will be out at the course by early afternoon.  If you are able to come, shoot me an email letting me know you can come and your cell for contact.  We will probably need help right up to race start.

EventName: Roller Coaster of Love Bike Festival 2026
EventNotes:
https://www.norbatrails.org/rollercoastermtbfest

Race Format (3/6 Hour Race):

  • The rider who completes the most laps within the time limit (3 or 6 hours) will be declared the winner and will podium.
  • In the event of a tie, the fastest time to complete the tied number of laps will determine the winner.
  • If available, a scoreboard will be updated at the timing tent throughout the race.
  • A large digital clock at the finish line will display the remaining race time.
  • Laps completed after the time limit has expired will not be counted.
  • After completing a lap, riders may begin another lap, take a break or stop racing.
  • Completing at least one lap is required to avoid a DNF (Did Not Finish).
  • Riders may forfeit a lap at any time and return to the trailhead, but must report to the timing tent and inform race officials.
  • The race will begin in waves.
  • Wave size and start times will be determined by the Timing Officials.
  • Riders compete individually, teamwork is not allowed.

Race Format (Time Trial):

  • Individual Start – Riders start one at a time at set intervals (e.g., 30 sec or 1 min).
  • Course – Short trail course for XC. Pump track and Dual slalom courses are located near the trailhead.
  • Timing – Each rider is timed; fastest time wins.
  • Passing – Slower riders must yield if caught; good trail etiquette is essential.
  • Riders compete individually, teamwork is not allowed.

General XC Rules

  1. Equipment:
    • All riders must wear a bicycle helmet at all times while on the course. Failure to do so will result in disqualification.
    • Bikes must be mountain bikes suitable for off-road trails and equipped with a front and rear brake.
    • Race numbers must be visible on the handlebar area of the bike at all times.
  2. Conduct and Etiquette:
    • Racers must race respectfully and announce their intentions when passing another rider on the trail.
    • Cheating of any kind may result in disqualification at the discretion of the Timing Officials.
    • Abusive language, unsportsmanlike behavior, or deliberate obstruction of other riders will result in penalties or disqualification.
  3. Course Rules:
    • Riders must stay on the marked course at all times.
    • Cutting the course or taking shortcuts will result in disqualification.
    • If a rider encounters mechanical issues, they must move off the main trail to make repairs to avoid obstructing other participants.
  4. Safety:
    • Racers will be disqualified for racing without a bicycle helmet.
    • If a rider is seriously injured, the nearest rider must stop to offer assistance and report the incident to race officials. Call 911 if a rider is unconscious or unresponsive. 
    • For riders that have minor injuries, please inform the timing officials and we will send a representative onto the race course to assist. 
  5. Assistance and Support:
    • Racers may only receive assistance from non-racers in the staging area.
    • Racers may help other racers out on the course.
    • Racers are responsible for their own nutrition and hydration while on the course. Water will be available in the staging area.
  6. Penalties and Disqualification:
    • Timing Officials have the authority to disqualify racers for cheating, unsportsmanlike conduct, or safety violations.
    • Racers who intentionally cut the course or take shortcuts will be disqualified.
  7. Protests:
    • Any protests regarding race results or conduct must be filed with race officials within 30 minutes of the race ending.
    • Decisions made by race officials are final.
  8. Miscellaneous:
    • Please ensure that your race number is clearly visible on your bike at all times.
    • Good sportsmanship is expected of all participants. Unacceptable behavior will not be tolerated.

 

Enduro MTB Race Rules

  1. Race Format:
    • The race will be competed in stages with each stage being approximately one minute of “downhill” riding.
  2. Course Inspection:
    • Each rider will have pre-ride time to inspect the course before the race begins.
  3. Timed Runs:
    • Each rider may only receive one timed run per stage, unless otherwise approved by timing officials due to exceptional circumstances.
    • In case of interruption, such as stopping to assist a downed rider or mechanical issue, riders may reattempt a timed run. Riders must notify the Timing Official of the forfeited run to get approval for a reattempt. 
    • Reattempts for mechanical issues will be at the discretion of the race officials
  4. Assisting Downed Riders:
    • Riders are encouraged to check on and help downed riders.
    • If a rider stops to assist, they may have the opportunity to reattempt their timed run for that stage. The interruption must be reported to the Timing Official immediately.
  5. Safety:
    • Racers will be disqualified for racing without a bicycle helmet.
    • If a rider is seriously injured, the nearest rider must stop to offer assistance and report the incident to race officials. Call 911 if a rider is unconscious or unresponsive. 
    • For riders that have minor injuries, please inform the timing officials and we will send a representative onto the race course to assist. 
    • All riders must wear a helmet. Additional protective gear such as knee pads, elbow pads, and gloves are highly encouraged.
  6. Conduct:
    • Riders must act responsibly, showing good sportsmanship at all times.
    • Cheating, unsportsmanlike behavior, or any form of interference with other riders will result in penalties or disqualification.
  7. Course Rules:
    • Riders must stay on the marked course at all times.
    • Cutting the course or taking shortcuts will result in disqualification.
    • Mechanical issues must be resolved off the main trail to avoid interfering with other participants.
  8. Technical Assistance:
    • Riders may only receive assistance from non-racers in designated support areas.
    • Assistance with mechanical repairs from other riders on the course is permitted but must not interfere with other participants.
  9. Protests and Disqualification:
    • Any protests regarding race results or conduct must be filed with race officials within 30 minutes of the stage or race ending.
    • Decisions made by race officials are final.
    • Violations of the above rules will result in penalties or disqualification at the discretion of the race officials.

 

Ebike Rules for All Events

  1. Eligibility:
    • Only Class 1 Ebikes with a maximum of 750 watts and a 20 mph speed limiter are permitted unless otherwise agreed upon by vote from all participants.
  2. Motor Assistance:
    • Ebikes must be pedal assist only.
    • The motor cannot rely on a throttle to engage; it must assist the rider based on pedaling.
  3. Battery Rules:
    • The Ebike battery cannot be switched out during the event unless agreed upon by all participants to ensure fairness in battery consumption between different manufacturers and motor types.
    • Battery extenders are allowed on Ebikes with batteries under 500 watt-hours (wh).
    • Battery extenders and battery changes may be permitted for batteries over 500wh at the discretion of race officials, due to excessive reduction in battery capacity (e.g., old battery). This rule must also be agreed upon by all participants to account for the wide variety in bike manufacturers and battery types.
  4. Equipment and Safety:
    • All standard race rules and equipment requirements apply to Ebike riders, including mandatory helmet use and visible race numbers.
    • Riders must follow all course rules and remain on the designated trail.
  5. Conduct and Etiquette:
    • Ebike riders must race respectfully and announce their intentions when passing another rider on the trail.
    • Cheating or modifications to the Ebike to exceed the power or speed limits will result in disqualification.
  6. Technical Assistance:
    • Riders may only receive assistance from non-racers in the staging area.
    • Ebike riders may help other Ebike riders out on the course as long as it does not violate other rules.
  7. Protests and Disqualification:
    • Any violations of the above rules that give undue advantage, such as unauthorized battery changes or throttle use, will result in disqualification.
    • Rider protests regarding Ebike issues must be filed with race officials within 30 minutes of the race ending.
    • Decisions made by race officials are final.

EventName: Clydesdale Hill Climb - Driftless Gravel Festival
The Grind - Junior MTB Races at Mt Van Hoevenberg
EventNotes:
The Grind  Mountain Bike race has something for junior aged riders (18 and younger) of all experience levels. The races are part of the Whoop UCI Mountain Bike World Series Lake Placid events. Races will start and finish under the World Series gantry, just like the pros. Riders can choose to race one to three laps of a 2 mile (3.5 km) race course. The course has mostly wide and fast cross country ski trail segments along with two sections of twisty single track. It includes one major uphill. 

Whoop UCI Mountain Bike World Series Event Tickets  - All racers, family and friends will need an event ticket to access the venue on race day. Event tickets are not included with the race entry fee. Tickets can be purchased here.

Parking -  Parking on venue requires a permit. One permit per entry will be included in the race fee. Racers will be directed to a designated parking area.  The parking permit is good for Friday only. You will not be allowed into the Expo, Paddock or Spectator areas with a bike. Please keep your bike with your vehicle when spectating.

Number Plate Pick Up - Pick up number plates and transponders at the North Plaza of the Mountain Pass Lodge 12:00 to 1:30.

Course Access - The course, minus the start finish area, will open for riding begining at 11:00 am. The full course will be open at 1:30 pm.

Start Procedure -  Racers load into the start at the far end of the UCI Pit zone at 1:50 Expert races will be called to the start first, then Intermediate racers, then Beginners racers. Experts will start at 2:00, after that, Intermediates will move forward and start at 2:01, after that, Beginners will move forward and start at 2:02.

Pit - There is no designated pit area, but the race course will pass by the parking area. You can pit in this area.

Call Up - Expert Racers can request a call up position by completing this form.

Results – Live results will be posted to Underdog Race Timing.

Awards - The top three finishers in two year age groups will be awarded in a ceremony on the UCI stage at 3:00.

 Award winners wait to be called on the stage side of the race course - family and friends will have the best photo opportunity on the opposite side of the race course. 

Expert race award categories - U12, U14, U16, U18 

Intermediate race award categories - U10, U12, U14, U16, U18. 

Beginner race award categories - U8, U10, U12, U14, & U16.

SINGLESPEED GRAVEL CHAMPIONSHIPS

Pay Nothing. Give Everything.
v.2026.10.03

Key Points:

  1. Pay Nothing. Give Everything. We are keeping the costs low and the expectations high.
  2. For ‘26 we’re keeping the same racy 55.5 mile distance but on a NEW ROUTE.
  3. Adding a NEW 33.3 mile FUN RIDE distance and gears are welcome! No podiums or fancy trophies, just fun.
  4. If you register and later decide not to participate, please edit your entry in BikeReg and move yourself to the category “I'm OUT - I can no longer participate.” Thanks in advance.
  5. Registration is open on BikeReg until a night or two before race day (and it's free) so no “day of” registration. Renegade if you want but no podium for you. We got stuff to do on race day and don't have time to bend our lives to your poor planning.

Schedule:

  • Saturday, October 3, 2025, Cumming, Iowa, at The Cumming Tap (117 N 44th St, Cumming, IA 50061)
  • 9a: check-in at The Cumming Tap and then gather yourself for the best singlespeed gravel race/ride of your life.
  • 9:45a: ease your way to the shiny brand new Cumming Main Street and then to the adjacent gravel Whatever Street for the start line and a few final minutes of self-doubt. Check your tires even though it's too late. Look for people who appear to know what they're doing and go to them.
  • 10a: Give Everything.
  • Sometime later…podiums and championship Wrangler flannel jerseys followed by pride and joy.

Rules (the written kind):

  1. You must be present to win.
  2. Bolt-on aero bars are not allowed.
  3. Yep, singlespeed bikes only (gears are welcome on the FUN RIDE).
  4. No outside support unless available to all racers. Racers may support other racers. And probably should.
  5. Each racer must have a pre-assigned friend/enemy to come pick them up in case of an issue. There is no transportation available from the race director. If you don’t show at the finish no one will come looking for you. YOU ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR YOU. 

Route

  1. Routes (subject to change so never “save to my routes” until you know they are final):
    1. 55.5 Mile Championship
    2. 33.3 Mile Fun Ride
  2. Course will not be marked. We will have a crack staff of volunteers at the key spots. Don’t trust the RWGPS ascent estimates cuz they are always low by a gazillion percent (roughly 25%). Plan on 4K feet of climb.
  3. There is a convenience store on the Championship route in St Charles, and we'll have a couple spots to breathe life back into yourself with liquids and calories.
  4. There are no formal checkpoints, so you do NOT need to stop anywhere on the course - this is a race with championships on the line! Make sure to cross the various chipless timing mats out there for accurate splits for the real-time closed circuit satellite feed to The Cumming Tap. Wave to the hidden cameras.
  5. Some beautiful B road are on the route. They can be smooth, sketchy, mud, or a combination of all 3. Be careful.
  6. The route is hard and you’re dumb to do it. Do not attempt this race unless you have previously ridden a similar distance on singlespeed on hilly gravel and not died. Not kidding…it is hard.
  7. Tires & gravel conditions…the gravel roads on the route are LIMESTONE with a firm base so you don’t need big ‘ol tires unless you like how they roll. No sandy/pebble roads. The B roads are dirt and fast when dry - just gotta be careful of washouts/ruts. There will likely be fresh gravel here and there to dash your hopes and sidewalls.
  8. Chipless timing provided by Sundial Chrono.

Quitting:

  1. Call/text your pre-assigned friend/enemy to come get you because no one else will.
  2. Call/text Chris Kyhl so he also knows you’re OUT @ 515-554-7024.
  3. No one who does this race is a quitter. Unless you quit. Consider chasing the DFL Championship Jersey instead.

Podiums:

  1. Big budget podiums with trophies to write home about. Fastest person in each cat is the champ. That’s how bike races work.
  2. DFL Champ. Finish DFL without cutting course or getting a ride or any other sort of cheating and win a Wrangler champ jersey just like the winners which clearly indicates you were DFL. Wear around town amongst your gravel singlespeeding circle and impress those losers. You clearly worked harder than anyone else and deserve a DFL Champ jersey more than the overall winner. Mainly because they won and you were DFL.
  3. KOM. This was new in ‘25 and worked well. Probably do something similar in ‘26. Or, maybe we’ll do a Green Points Flannel with some intermediate sprints. You never know

It’s time to turn the volume up to 111!

The Pisgah 111 is the quintessential crusher of a cross-country endurance MTB race. Racers follow a 65.1 mile course with 10,200' feet of climbing along the most iconic trails and gravel roads known in Pisgah National Forest. Just peek at the course map and list of trails and you’ll immediately get chills just thinking about the epic scenery and terrain you’ll encounter.

This is a true mountain bike race with no map reading skills required, just follow the arrows. Think of it as the most exciting (and grueling) tour of Pisgah you can imagine during the peak of the leaves changing in the forest. 

It certainly wouldn’t hurt to study the map and cue sheets to know what you’re getting yourself into, as some of these trails will test your lungs and your legs while the scenery blows your mind.

There will be FOUR rest areas (at three locations) along the way that will be stocked with water, food (PB&J, fruit, salty snacks, sweet snacks,  bars), first aid, and neutral mechanical support. Riders may send drop bags to each rest area. Be sure to read the information below, too. 

Not enough racing for you? Register for the entire King and Queen of Pisgah series!

Year 12~ Can You Beleive IT! ~Vermont Rare Gravel!

Happy to see have you back for another year!  You'll see some new, some old and somewhere in between.  Keeping it around 40miles this year….but we're turning up the climbing on a few new roads.  

Why not #vermontraregravelride this Year?

   


"Grassroots GRavel" at its Finest! 

It's not a Race, It's an Adventure!  

The Hidden Gem of Southern VT

Use your GPS - minimal signage

Start/Finish and post ride gathering at Wild Wings XC ski center

 
 

What to Expect 

This is not a Race, However the front usually has Pace, But fast or slow LET'S obey the rules of the road = Don't be a Dick!  12th year running back to our original distance of 40 miles, 4500 vertical feet of climbing with 5 sections of good ole VT Class IV.  The most challenging could be the 19% up Johnson Hill Road.  40mm plus tires and gearing to keep your legs fresh are recommended.     

 

Ride Description and Profile - 2025, Good chance this is It!

https://www.strava.com/routes/3399914793929721038

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/52379474

 

Highlights include 

  • New Class IV section; Turner Road - Highway 26 to Moses Pond
  • Middletown Road to Marsh Hill
  • Johnson Hill is back - Sorry!
  • Little Michigan to Stone Place
  • Hapgood Pond Campground to North Road

There are a few short sections that some riders may want to dismount and walk or jog.  And that's Okay, go  your own pace; the challenge is as important as the journey!  

*  As we did in 2020 We will be adhering to the Vermont State Covid guidelines if required.  https://accd.vermont.gov/covid-19/restart/cross-state-travel   Please mask if you are not vaccinated and keep your 6 feet of distance.   

 

Equipment Recommendation

This ride is calling for cross, gravel, flat bar mountain, or the like ~highly discourage any road bikes!  38 cc and above tire choice will serve you well.  There is no "hike-a-bike" ALL totally ridable Class IV.

Water + Food

There will be 2 refueling/ Feed stations; one at 14 miles (top of Marsh Cross and Dale Road) and 28 miles at the top of Holt Mtn Class IV stocked with GU gels, GU hydration, bananas, pickles, syrup shots and more. We do recommend you carry plenty of water and your own nutrition as well.  

Race day parking

Plenty of parking at Wild Wings Nordic Center.  Follow Hapgood Road east out of Peru Center.  At the town garage bear left onto North Road.  Follow North Rd. appox. 2 miles, bear left at the folk, 500 meters to Wild Wings XC.

Ride with a Purpose - All Proceeds go to Rare Disease Research and Advocacy

I started this endeavor twelve years ago as a passionate cyclist with a cause.  Building community, Advocating for a cause, challenged with the parallels between gravel riding/ racing, walking the rare disease journey and educating myself and others, about childhood rare disease.  I am not a charity but work directly with Vermont Rare, Rasopathies Network, CFC International amongst others to educate people on rare disease and finding ways to improve the lives of young people and families that live with a rare disease.  So if you to are passionate about something, enjoy strong community and friends, do things with a purpose, love to ride and are excited about a new challenge, Vermont Rare Gravel might be the perfect fit!

Welcome to the 2026 Driftless Gravel Festival!

We have teamed up with the ultra distance race, the Driftless Dagger, to form a weekend long festival in the most underrated cycling destination the Midwest. The party will get started on Friday afternoon with shakeout rides, a kids race, and packet pick up. The festival will take place at Chestnut Mountain Resort which is located in the heart of Driftless country while also overlooking the Mighty Mississippi.

 The Galena territory was founded by resilient, industrious folks who put the area on the map by being the first major site of the mineral rush in the United States. They mined over 21 million pounds of lead in just a 3 year period. If you want to finish The Lead Ore, you’ll need the same tenacity that these early pioneers demonstrated. The Lead Ore will take place from Chestnut Mountain Resort which is situated smack dab in the middle of the Illinois driftless region. This is arguably the most scenic region Illinois has to offer. If you have never been to the Galena area, you're in for a surprise. The area offers many activities for couples and families. We recommend making a weekend out of this one and taking in the full experience. There are no refunds or deferrals. BikeReg does offer registration insurance at checkout.

Cycle 66 does not happen without a small army of volunteers!  There's a place for everyone. Be sure to check out the information below for each of the volunteer roles. Free T-Shirts for volunteers who sign-up before September 15th!

SATURDAY, OCTOBER 3RD - PRE-EVENT DAY NEEDS

Packet Pickup Team:
We are thrilled that Packet Pickup will be located at Frenzy Brewing Co., in Downtown Edmond. Join us as we get the Cycle 66 party started. This team will handout T-shirts, rider info and smiles to registrants throughout the day Saturday, between 11am and 6pm. Sign-up for one or more shifts.

  • Three Shifts Available: 10:30am to 1pm / 1pm to 3:30pm / 3:30pm to 6pm
  • 12 people needed per shift
  • Supplies and information provided
  • Cycle 66 staff will be on-hand to answer rider questions

Course Marking Team:
Cycle 66 riders rely on the efforts of the Course Marking Team to place directional arrows and signs along the routes. Access to a vehicle (preferably an SUV or a pickup truck) with space for signs and stands is suggested. Course marking is completed on Saturday evening prior to the Ride. The entire route is usually marked in about 4 hours.

  • 2pm to 6pm
  • 8 people needed (will work in teams of 2)
  • Ride Director will supply detailed maps and instructions

SUNDAY, OCTOBER 4TH - EVENT DAY NEEDS

Rest Stop Team

Crit Course Team

SAG (Support & Gear) Team:
Rider safety is a big part of Cycle 66, and this team helps our riders out on the road! A personal vehicle with a bike rack (or a truck or SUV) is required. (We may be able to loan you a rack for the day.) This team is responsible for patrolling the route within assigned zones to make sure riders are safe. This could include picking up broken-down cyclists, calling for the medical team in the case of an injury, or reporting back to the ride director about any dangerous situations that may arise. Takes place all-day Sunday, but shifts may be available, so please reach out if that works better for you. Expect a virtual training session the week of the event.

  • 7am to 2pm (shorter shifts available by request)
  • Twelve (12) Licensed Drivers needed
  • Basic supplies will be provided
  • Truck/SUV or vehicle with bike rack required
  • Virtual training session week before the event

EventName: Fon Solo Gravel/Last Standing/Cider Cross (Maine Gravel Series)
EventNotes:
Cider Cross / Fon Solo Weekend 2026! 

Year Five — Bigger, Better, and More Fun Than Ever!
[October 3-4| Alna, ME]

Forget the pumpkin spice — we’ve got a sour batch of apples ready to be mashed!

Join us for a two-day festival of fall mayhem featuring short-track MTB & CX racing, last-person-standing style trail running, epic gravel rides, and camping under the stars. Whether you're racing, riding, running, or just hanging out by the fire, Cider Cross / Fon Solo has something for everyone.

SATURDAY: CIDER CROSS + BACKYARD ULTRA-STYLE RUN

Cider Cross Race:

  • One 40-minute race with CX and MTB categories
  • About a 1-mile course – re-routed for 2025 to feature faster, more open gravel-friendly sections
  • Expect slop, speed, and heckling
  • Bring any bike — gravel, mountain, cyclocross — whatever rolls!
  • Yes, the optional fire jump is back.
  • Yes, there will be prizes (top 3 per category, TBD)

Last-Person-Standing Trail Run:

  • Race format an easier version of the Backyard Ultra
  • ~1 mile loops on the same course
  • Time limit decreases by 1 minute per lap
    (e.g., Lap 1 = 20 min, Lap 2 = 19 min, etc.)
  • Run till you can't make the cutoff!
  • You can expect 7–8 laps if you're at a 12-min/mile pace
  • Last year, the fastest runners made it down to the 6-minute mark!

Food, drinks, and camping available.

BYOBreakfast! (But seriously, sign up for a camping spot early.)

SUNDAY: THE FON SOLO GRAVEL LOOP

Our grand finale — a gravel adventure through the Sheepscot Valley. This year, we’ve got two route options:

  • Short Loop: ~25 miles — easier & faster than the original loop. Fewer climbs, smoother ride, great for the gravel curious.
  • Full Loop: ~49 miles — the classic, with climbs, views, and chunky gravel madness.  The route will be very similar to last year but we are always looking for areas of improvement!
  • Less full Loop ~41 miles.  The same as the full loop with the furthest 8 miles trimmed off. 

Both routes:

  • Cruise scenic roads and remote stretches of backcountry beauty
  • Roll through the tasting deck at Oxbow Brewing near the finish (yes, seriously)
  • End with good vibes, sore legs, and cold cider

REGISTRATION INFO:

  • Open to ALL — racers, riders, runners, and revelers
  • Sign up for one day, both, or just come hang out!
  • Spots are limited, and we WILL sell out — don't wait!

All proceeds go to support The Schmid Preserve in Edgecomb.
Ride, run, and race for a great cause.

 

New this year…we have merch available!  There is a selection of T's, a hoodie and trucker hat to choose from!  You can order directly from Hubnotic and your items will ship to you directly.    https://www.hubnotic.com/collections/fon-solo 50% of all orders benefit the Schmid Preserve!

Prepare for an unforgettable cycling adventure in the heart of the Midwest. Whether you're a seasoned gravel racer or a casual rider seeking scenic thrills, our event promises an exhilarating experience for all.

The Old Fashioned Gravel ride/race is back for 2026! We are fortunate enough to have some of the best gravel riding in the Midwest and have put together four routes to show off the local terrain. As with all of our rides, we offer a little bit of everything and welcome EVERYONE from novice riders to the most seasoned racers. The focus of the ride is to bring like-minded individuals together for a great ride, but we will have professional timing so if you want to race we will have you covered too! Routes that will satisfy all of your gravely desires, and a post-ride gathering with food, drink, and hangs with new friends. Awards and prizes (everything from ridiculous to awesome) to follow the ride!

We will once again be at a venue in Hokah Minnesota, a rustic farm nestled in a scenic coulee. While the ride is about riding with other rad people like yourself, rest assured a portion of your entry fee will go to a local entity that could use a little financial help. If we can have a super fun time while helping others, that is what will make this a successful event. Hokah is a super cool little town, and we would love to help keep our money local.

All routes will leave and finish at the farm. The gravel is approximately two miles from the start line, and one mile of that is a paved climb, once you are on the ridge, the dust shall start flying! All routes will descend this paved section upon return to the finish line.

The Driftless Dagger is a self-supported bikepacking race through the rugged, untamed beauty of the Driftless Region. Choose between a grueling 550-mile route with over 40,000 feet of climbing or the Baby Dagger at 237 miles with 20,000 feet of vert. Starting and finishing at Chestnut Mountain Resort in Galena, IL, this race is Death by a Thousand Cuts—relentless gravel, brutal climbs, and peaceful back roads that challenge your limits.
